title: Copernicus Marine KD490 as the attenuation of the water-column-corrected branch
status_note: Not registered. The fallback rule and the pass criteria are open decisions; no corrected-branch result with CMEMS attenuation may be computed before they are fixed here.
question: With an attenuation taken from outside the image, does the water-column-corrected branch, unavailable in v1, predict July cover better than depth alone?
why: In v1 the QAA fit over the Pleiades Neo deep-water reference raised plausibility flags on both dates (red_reference_selected(655nm), bbp_555_implausible; Kd(486) 1.32 and 1.26 m-1), so the registered rule left the corrected branch unavailable (archive/out/optics-reference/runs/20260920T115500-a5823dc0e7cc/reference_iops.json).

attenuation_source.pixel: the valid KD490 pixel nearest the quadrat cluster (38.409 N, 9.202 W), searched within 5 km and 3 days

spectral_extension.shape: E5s median non-water absorption and particulate backscatter (forced-560 QAA, Sentinel-2, 24 December 2025 and 22 February 2026)
spectral_extension.magnitude: one factor on that shape, chosen so that the Lee et al. (2005) Kd(490) of the scaled IOPs equals the CMEMS value
spectral_extension.library: oceanstream.coastal at c3dc02a (pure-water optics and the Kd model)

open_decisions: When CMEMS stands in: always when the in-scene QAA is flagged, or only when the CMEMS match passes thresholds on distance, day offset and uncertainty (3 September carries 84 %).
Which correction consumes the IOPs: the Lee inversion of the library, or the Lyzenga-style ratio of r1.
The pass criterion: for example, the r1 recovery rule (MAE at least 2 percentage points below depth-only, July leave-one-transect-out), and whether September is evaluated.
The scenes: Pleiades Neo 8 July and 3 September; whether the clean Sentinel-2 dates (2 July, 31 August) are added.
known_limits: The pixel is 1 km across and lies 0.29 km from the reef, near cliffs and partly over optically shallow water: adjacency light and bottom reflectance can bias it.
A correct attenuation does not remove the radiometric residual of 0.01 to 0.04 that r1 to r6 found as large as the seabed contrast; the correction amplifies that residual by exp(K z).
Two winter dates compare CMEMS with the in-scene QAA that passed: 0.090 against 0.13 (24 December 2025) and 0.271 against 0.20 (22 February 2026).
